text:
maria: Quick check — we have a handful of legacy clients that don't set Accept-Model. If we flip the default model in prod, what will their behavior be? do they get the new default or stay on the old one?

arjun: They get the default model at the server side unless they explicitly pin. So flip => new model for unpinned.

tim: Is there an existing grace path? I'd prefer we avoid surprise regressions for embedded devices.

maria: Exactly. Need to know if we can do a phased rollout or an automatic shim.

lee: We built a lightweight compatibility probe in the runtime last quarter — it can detect important response-shape diffs and route to a fallback variant. But it's off for default flips currently.

arjun: Technically we can enable the probe for a percentage of traffic (canary) and have it fallback to the pinned-compatible variant on regressions.

julie: Timeline ask from CS: customers with strict contracts want 60 days notice + opt-out. Can we support that?

arjun: Yes — rollout plan: (1) announce deprecation window 60d, (2) enable probe in 5% canary, (3) ramp with automated regression gates, (4) 2-week extended opt-out via account metadata.

maria: For the opt-out, how do we express it in the API? header, account flag, or both?

lee: Prefer account flag (control plane) for enterprise customers. Header (Accept-Model) for clients that can change quickly. We'll expose both: Accept-Model and account-level pin.

arjun: Implementation detail: account pin takes precedence over header to avoid accidental client overrides.

sam: Ops note — enabling the probe at scale affects KV cache invalidation patterns. Expect a ~3% throughput delta on some model sizes. Need capacity heads up.

maria: Good call. Sam can you throw an estimate into the rollout ticket?

sam: Yep, I'll add numbers and a throttle plan by EOD.

maria: For devs working on the client SDKs, please add an opt-in flag to set Accept-Model and a compatibility test that verifies response envelope keys. lightweight check is fine.

tim: I'll drop a stub PR for the SDK toggles and the test harness. ping me for reviews.

arjun: One more: what about streaming responses? the probe currently compares final envelope; streaming diffs can be trickier.

lee: For streaming, probe will validate initial envelope + a token-sample checksum after N tokens. If mismatch, fallback will terminate stream and reissue against fallback model. We agreed this behavior in the design doc.

maria: Cool. Action items: arjun add canary config + gates, lee enable probe toggle + streaming checksum, sam capacity numbers, tim SDK PR, julie comms draft for 60d notice. I'll coordinate with CS.

compat-bot: Reminder: created ticket INF-4721 "default-model-flip: compatibility rollout" assigned to @arjun, @lee, @sam.

julie: Thx — I'll start the customer cadence doc. Can we get a short checklist for what to include in the notice?

arjun: Include: what changes, affected endpoints, opt-out instructions, timeline, rollback plan, and contact for regressions.

maria: Perfect. If no objections we'll start the 60-day clock after the canary is healthy. :thumbsup:

tim: no objections from me. will review SDK PR quickly.

lee: zero objections. i'll prep the probe toggle PR.

sam: all good. I'll post capacity numbers in the ticket when ready.

maria: thanks everyone — closing the loop here. Will post the rollout doc link once it's live.
